findings.issue_text: P1: Goroutines derive 10s timeout from the request context; once the handler returns, the canceled parent context immediately cancels the legacy write with 'context canceled', making legacy writes in Mode 3 racy/unreliable

P2: Legacy-side errors are silently swallowed in all four goroutines; the previous log.Error calls for legacy failures were removed, so a failing legacy store diverges silently with no operator signal beyond a metric
P2: Update passes raw objInfo to Legacy.Update instead of the updateWrapper-wrapped object that was written to storage, causing potential divergence between legacy and storage stores
P2: Update error path calls recordLegacyDuration when the storage update fails; it should call recordStorageDuration, misattributing storage failures to legacy metrics
P2: DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration inside the legacy goroutine; it should be recordLegacyDuration, corrupting both metric series
P3: Delete success path passes object name instead of options.Kind as the kind label to recordStorageDuration, breaking metric aggregation/dashboards

P2: Tests share one Prometheus registry after removal of the local prometheus.NewRegistry(), risking duplicate metrics collector registration panics or cross-test contamination; also TestMode3_Create/Delete/DeleteCollection spawn legacy goroutines whose results aren't awaited, causing flaky assertions

P3: Delete/DeleteCollection semantics change is undocumented: async return from Storage.Delete is returned while legacy deletion runs concurrently with deleteValidation executed after the response, possibly in a canceled context

Goroutines in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection derive from request context via context.WithTimeoutCause, so legacy writes are cancelled when the request completes; should use context.Background() or context.WithoutCancel(ctx) as base
Unbounded per-request goroutine spawning with no concurrency control (limiter, semaphore, or queue) causes memory pressure scaling with write rate × legacy latency
No WaitGroup for background goroutines, so in-flight legacy writes are silently dropped on process shutdown causing divergence
Background legacy DeleteCollection can materialize an arbitrarily large result set concurrently with no cap, allowing multiple concurrent bulk deletes to stack load on the legacy store
DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration for the legacy operation, corrupting metrics
Delete passes name instead of options.Kind as the kind label to the metric recorder
Update records recordLegacyDuration on a storage failure, skewing latency metrics and masking real legacy-side issues

Update goroutine passes raw objInfo to Legacy.Update instead of the object returned by Storage.Update, allowing legacy copy to diverge from unified copy (wrong resourceVersion → update conflicts, stale data)
Legacy write failures in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection goroutines are completely silent — errors only recorded as metrics, no log.Error, event, or alerting path

Goroutines derive 10s timeout from the request context, so client disconnect after unified write cancels the legacy write entirely — needs a detached context (context.WithoutCancel/background + timeout)
Delete success path passes object name where a kind is expected in recordStorageDuration, polluting the kind metric label with object names (cardinality explosion)
DeleteCollection goroutine uses recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy timings to storage
Update storage-error path calls recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, counting storage failures as legacy
No circuit-breaker/rate limiting/failure-rate tracking or reconciliation queue for fire-and-forget legacy writes, leading to unbounded goroutine growth and silent divergence during legacy outage

Delete no longer tolerates legacy NotFound errors, inflating failure metrics for objects never migrated

P1: Async legacy writes in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection use the inbound request context via context.WithTimeoutCause, which is cancelled once the handler returns, so legacy writes almost always run on a done context and fail; should use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or context.Background()
P2: DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy delete-collection latency/errors to the storage metric
P2: Update error path records a storage update failure via recordLegacyDuration (copy/paste error), skewing both metrics
P2: Async legacy goroutines are untracked (no WaitGroup) so writes can be lost on shutdown, and concurrent legacy writes race on shared request state via createValidation/updateValidation closures
P2: Tests TestMode3_Create/Update/Delete never assert lsSpy counts or m.AssertExpectations, so async legacy dual-writes are effectively untested (goroutine may not run before test ends)

P2: Update no longer fetches old object and computes UpdatedObject/wraps in updateWrapper, passing raw objInfo to legacy Update, changing what legacy storage receives and validation semantics, without test coverage
P2: Delete no longer tolerates apierrors.IsNotFound from unified storage and returns immediately, breaking deletes when unified storage is missing an object that exists in legacy
P3: Delete records storage duration with object name instead of options.Kind as the kind label, producing inconsistent metric labels
P3: No test coverage for legacy-write failure while storage succeeds or the 10s WithTimeoutCause timeout firing; timeout and metric-recording paths have zero coverage
P3: TestMode3_Create failure case is mislabeled — only setupLegacyFn is configured and the storage mock is unset, so the intended unified-store failure path is not genuinely exercised

Async legacy writes in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection derive their 10s-timeout context from the request ctx, which is canceled when the HTTP response is written, so fire-and-forget legacy writes will frequently be canceled before completing, silently diverging legacy vs unified storage

Update no longer reconciles the legacy write with the stored object: raw objInfo is passed to d.Legacy.Update instead of the updateWrapper carrying the object persisted to unified storage, so defaults/mutations (RV bump, normalization) never reach legacy, causing persistent divergence
Legacy write failures are silently dropped with no logging; errors are only fed into a metric, removing the previous log.Error trace and making divergence undiagnosable in production
Update error path calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) (~line 145) instead of recordStorageDuration, polluting the legacy latency metric with unified-storage failures

DeleteCollection legacy goroutine calls d.recordStorageDuration(...) (~line 175) instead of recordLegacyDuration, so the legacy metric never gets delete-collection data and the storage metric is double-counted
Delete passes name instead of options.Kind as the metric label (~line 108), mixing object names with kinds and breaking label consistency/cardinality for successful deletes

Goroutines capture options/deleteValidation/objInfo and re-run createValidation/deleteValidation asynchronously after the response; if validations depend on request-scoped state or have side effects, behavior differs from the synchronous path
Massive duplication of the timing/logging/async pattern across five methods, which already introduced copy-paste bugs (wrong recorder, wrong label); a writeToLegacyAsync helper would prevent these

Tests reuse a shared package-level p registry while TestMode3_Get creates a fresh local one; if the shared registry is a package global reused across test functions, metric registration may panic with duplicate metrics collector registration
mode3Str const is declared after first use (~line 33) and the mode string is duplicated per mode file, adding per-method metric-label plumbing as more mode files are added

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Goroutines derive 10s timeout from the request context; once the handler returns, the canceled parent context immediately cancels the legacy write with 'context canceled', making legacy writes in Mode 3 racy/unreliable

adjudication.rationale: In Mode 3, legacy writes are dispatched asynchronously but the goroutines derive their timeout context from the incoming request context (e.g., `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10*time.Second, ...) ... d.Legacy.Create(ctx, ...) }()` in `Create`, similarly in `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection`). Since these methods return immediately after starting the goroutine, the parent request context is likely canceled when the handler returns, causing the derived context to be canceled early and making legacy operations racy/unreliable (often failing with `context canceled`) despite the 10s timeout.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Legacy-side errors are silently swallowed in all four goroutines; the previous log.Error calls for legacy failures were removed, so a failing legacy store diverges silently with no operator signal beyond a metric

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy-side operations were changed to run asynchronously in goroutines for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection, and those goroutines record metrics via recordLegacyDuration but do not log errors. Previously, legacy failures were logged (e.g., Create: log.WithValues(...).Error; Delete: log.WithValues(...).Error; Update: log.Error; DeleteCollection: log.WithValues(...).Error). In the new goroutines, errors like `errObjectSt` / `err` are not passed to `log.Error(...)`, so legacy write failures can occur without an immediate operator-visible log signal (beyond metrics). This is an observability/regression concern rather than a direct functional correctness bug in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Update passes raw objInfo to Legacy.Update instead of the updateWrapper-wrapped object that was written to storage, causing potential divergence between legacy and storage stores

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the old implementation ensured Legacy received the exact object written to Storage by wrapping `objInfo` in an `updateWrapper` containing the `updated` object. The new implementation calls `d.Storage.Update(...)` and then asynchronously calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` (raw `objInfo`) without wrapping or otherwise ensuring it uses the Storage-written object. This can cause Legacy to compute a different updated object than Storage did, leading to divergence between the two stores (the exact scenario the prior `updateWrapper` prevented).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Update error path calls recordLegacyDuration when the storage update fails; it should call recordStorageDuration, misattributing storage failures to legacy metrics

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go` `Update(...)`, when `d.Storage.Update(...)` returns an error, the code records the duration via `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` even though this timing/error corresponds to the Storage update attempt (`startStorage` is taken before calling `d.Storage.Update`). This misattributes a storage failure to legacy metrics; it should call `recordStorageDuration` in that error path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration inside the legacy goroutine; it should be recordLegacyDuration, corrupting both metric series

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection`, the legacy-write goroutine ends with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` even though it is recording the legacy store operation duration (`d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)`). This should be `recordLegacyDuration(...)`; as written it attributes legacy timings/errors to the storage metric series (and omits the legacy series), corrupting metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Delete success path passes object name instead of options.Kind as the kind label to recordStorageDuration, breaking metric aggregation/dashboards

P2: Tests share one Prometheus registry after removal of the local prometheus.NewRegistry(), risking duplicate metrics collector registration panics or cross-test contamination; also TestMode3_Create/Delete/DeleteCollection spawn legacy goroutines whose results aren't awaited, causing flaky assertions

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes a per-test `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` in `dualwriter_mode1_test.go` while still passing `p` into `NewDualWriter(...)`, and several new Mode3 tests also call `NewDualWriter(..., p)` without creating a local registry (only `TestMode3_Get` creates one). That implies `p` is coming from shared/package scope, which can lead to cross-test metric registration contamination if `NewDualWriter` registers collectors on the provided registry. However, the claim about “flaky assertions” from Mode3’s legacy goroutines isn’t supported by this diff: the tests don’t assert legacy calls or await goroutine completion, so no assertions are directly made flaky here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Delete/DeleteCollection semantics change is undocumented: async return from Storage.Delete is returned while legacy deletion runs concurrently with deleteValidation executed after the response, possibly in a canceled context

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete` and `DeleteCollection`, the PR changes legacy-store operations from synchronous to asynchronous best-effort goroutines (e.g., `go func() { ... d.Legacy.Delete(ctx, name, deleteValidation, options) }()`). The handler returns `async` from `d.Storage.Delete(...)` immediately, so legacy deletion (and its `deleteValidation`) may run after the response and may not run at all if the parent `ctx` is canceled early (the goroutine uses `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`, which still inherits cancellation from `ctx`). This is a real, diff-grounded semantic change; whether it is a defect depends on intended guarantees/documentation, which is not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Goroutines in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection derive from request context via context.WithTimeoutCause, so legacy writes are cancelled when the request completes; should use context.Background() or context.WithoutCancel(ctx) as base

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, the async legacy operations in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection start goroutines that call context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...), where ctx is the request context (e.g., ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log)). Request contexts are typically canceled when the handler returns; since these legacy calls run after returning (in goroutines), they can be canceled immediately, preventing the intended legacy write/delete from happening in Mode3. This is directly visible in the new go func() blocks using the passed-in ctx as the parent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded per-request goroutine spawning with no concurrency control (limiter, semaphore, or queue) causes memory pressure scaling with write rate × legacy latency

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, Mode3 write paths now spawn a new goroutine per request to perform the legacy write asynchronously (e.g., `Create` uses `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.Create(...) }()`, similarly in `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection`). There is no limiter/semaphore/worker queue; under high write QPS and slow legacy storage, the number of in-flight goroutines can grow proportional to request rate × legacy latency/timeout (10s), creating real risk of resource exhaustion (memory/scheduler pressure) introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No WaitGroup for background goroutines, so in-flight legacy writes are silently dropped on process shutdown causing divergence

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes are moved into fire-and-forget goroutines in `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection` (e.g., `go func() { ... d.Legacy.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection(...) }()`), with no synchronization or shutdown coordination. This means the handler returns before the legacy write completes; on process shutdown, any in-flight goroutines can be terminated, and errors are not logged (only `recordLegacyDuration` is called), so legacy writes can be silently lost, causing divergence between Storage and Legacy despite comments stating mode 3 “writes to LegacyStorage and Storage.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: Background legacy DeleteCollection can materialize an arbitrarily large result set concurrently with no cap, allowing multiple concurrent bulk deletes to stack load on the legacy store

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection, the legacy delete is now launched in an unbounded goroutine (`go func() { ... d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...) }()`), with no concurrency limit or backpressure. Multiple concurrent DeleteCollection requests can therefore stack up background legacy DeleteCollection calls and overload the legacy store. The specific claim about “materialize an arbitrarily large result set” isn’t shown in the diff, but the unbounded concurrent bulk-delete behavior is directly introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration for the legacy operation, corrupting metrics

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, DeleteCollection launches a goroutine to perform the legacy delete: `_, err := d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)`, but then records the duration with `d.recordStorageDuration(...)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)` (see the go routine near the end of DeleteCollection). This will misattribute legacy-operation metrics to storage metrics, corrupting the intended metric breakdown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete passes name instead of options.Kind as the kind label to the metric recorder
Update records recordLegacyDuration on a storage failure, skewing latency metrics and masking real legacy-side issues

Update goroutine passes raw objInfo to Legacy.Update instead of the object returned by Storage.Update, allowing legacy copy to diverge from unified copy (wrong resourceVersion → update conflicts, stale data)

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Update now calls Storage.Update(...) and then asynchronously calls Legacy.Update(...) with the same original objInfo ("d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)") rather than an UpdatedObjectInfo wrapper that returns the object actually written to storage. The previous implementation explicitly wrapped objInfo to force legacy to write the exact object returned by Storage.Update. With the new code, legacy will recompute the updated object against legacy’s current state, which can diverge from the unified store’s result (e.g., resourceVersion/fields), causing conflicts/stale data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy write failures in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection goroutines are completely silent — errors only recorded as metrics, no log.Error, event, or alerting path

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes are now done asynchronously in goroutines for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection (e.g., `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.Create/...; d.recordLegacyDuration(err!=nil, ...) }()`), and those goroutines do not call `log.Error(...)` (or otherwise surface the error) when the legacy operation fails or times out—only metrics are recorded. The previous synchronous implementation logged legacy failures (e.g., Create logged `unable to create object in legacy storage`, Delete logged `could not delete from legacy store`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded observability/regression concern, but it doesn’t by itself prove a functional failure of the primary (Storage) path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Goroutines derive 10s timeout from the request context, so client disconnect after unified write cancels the legacy write entirely — needs a detached context (context.WithoutCancel/background + timeout)

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the async legacy operations (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) run in goroutines using `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...)` where `ctx` is the same request-derived context (only wrapped with klog via `klog.NewContext`). If the request context is canceled (e.g., client disconnects or handler returns and upstream cancels), the derived timeout context is canceled immediately, causing the legacy write/delete/update to be skipped/aborted. This defeats the intended “unified store sync + legacy async best-effort” behavior and matches the finding’s need for a detached context (e.g., `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or `context.Background()` + timeout).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete success path passes object name where a kind is expected in recordStorageDuration, polluting the kind metric label with object names (cardinality explosion)

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Delete(), the success path calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`, passing the object `name` as the third argument where other call sites consistently pass `options.Kind` (e.g., Create/Get/List/DeleteCollection). If that argument is the "kind" metric label, this will inject object names into the kind label, causing high-cardinality metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DeleteCollection goroutine uses recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy timings to storage

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, DeleteCollection launches a goroutine for the legacy delete: `_, err := d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)` but then records the duration with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`. This uses the storage metric recorder for a legacy operation, misattributing legacy timings to storage, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update storage-error path calls recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, counting storage failures as legacy
No circuit-breaker/rate limiting/failure-rate tracking or reconciliation queue for fire-and-forget legacy writes, leading to unbounded goroutine growth and silent divergence during legacy outage

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3, legacy writes are now done in fire-and-forget goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection all `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.*(...) }()`), with only a fixed 10s timeout via `context.WithTimeoutCause` and no rate limiting/circuit breaker/queueing. Under high request volume or a slow/failed legacy backend, this can lead to large numbers of concurrent goroutines in-flight (bounded only by request rate × timeout) and the caller will never see legacy failures. Additionally, the goroutines do not log legacy errors (they only call `recordLegacyDuration(...)`), so legacy outage can cause silent divergence beyond whatever the metrics provide.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fixed 10s legacy-write timeout hardcoded in all four goroutines without configurability; large collections or slow legacy backends will routinely exceed it

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, the legacy write/delete/update/delete-collection paths are executed asynchronously in goroutines and each wraps the legacy call with `context.WithTimeoutCause(..., time.Second*10, errors.New("legacy ... timeout"))` (Create, Delete, Update, DeleteCollection). The 10s timeout is hardcoded and not configurable anywhere in the diff, so the finding is accurate as a maintainability/operational concern. However, the diff does not prove this is a correctness defect (legacy operations are intentionally best-effort/async here), so it’s better classified as a non-bug review issue rather than a verifiable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete no longer tolerates legacy NotFound errors, inflating failure metrics for objects never migrated

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, the legacy delete is now performed asynchronously and its error is always treated as a failure for metrics: `_, _, err := d.Legacy.Delete(...)` followed by `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...)`. The previous implementation explicitly ignored `NotFound` via `apierrors.IsNotFound(errLS)` for legacy deletes. With the `apierrors` import removed and no `NotFound` check, legacy `NotFound` (e.g., object never written/migrated to legacy) will inflate failure metrics (and potentially alter error logging semantics).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Async legacy writes in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection use the inbound request context via context.WithTimeoutCause, which is cancelled once the handler returns, so legacy writes almost always run on a done context and fail; should use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or context.Background()

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3, the async legacy operations in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection spawn goroutines that derive their context from the inbound `ctx` via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` (e.g., `Create`: `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...); ... d.Legacy.Create(ctx, ...) }()`). Because these goroutines run after the main method returns, if the caller cancels the request context when the handler finishes, the parent `ctx` will already be done and the derived timeout context will be immediately canceled, causing legacy writes to fail or be skipped. The diff shows no use of `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or `context.Background()` to decouple the async work from request cancellation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy delete-collection latency/errors to the storage metric

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, DeleteCollection launches a goroutine to perform the legacy delete-collection call, but it records the duration via d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy) instead of using d.recordLegacyDuration(...). This verifiably misattributes legacy delete-collection latency/errors to the storage metric (the variable is even named startLegacy), unlike the other async legacy paths (Create/Delete/Update) which use recordLegacyDuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Update error path records a storage update failure via recordLegacyDuration (copy/paste error), skewing both metrics

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Update() measures startStorage then calls d.Storage.Update(...). On error, it logs "unable to update in storage" but records the duration via d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) instead of recordStorageDuration, misattributing a storage failure/latency to legacy metrics (copy/paste mistake).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Async legacy goroutines are untracked (no WaitGroup) so writes can be lost on shutdown, and concurrent legacy writes race on shared request state via createValidation/updateValidation closures

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3, legacy writes are now dispatched in `go func(){...}()` without any tracking/joining (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). They also derive the legacy context from the request `ctx` via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`, so if the request context is canceled when the handler returns, the async legacy operation can be canceled before it runs/completes. That makes it verifiable from the diff that legacy writes can be dropped even when the storage write succeeded, contradicting the mode3 comment (“writing to LegacyStorage and Storage”). The additional claim about races via validation closures is more speculative from the diff alone, but the untracked async + request-context-cancellation risk is a concrete correctness/data-loss issue introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Tests TestMode3_Create/Update/Delete never assert lsSpy counts or m.AssertExpectations, so async legacy dual-writes are effectively untested (goroutine may not run before test ends)

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes are now performed asynchronously via `go func() { ... d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection ... }()`. In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, the tests set up legacy expectations in some cases (e.g., `TestMode3_Create` and `TestMode3_Update` call `m.On("Create"/"Update", ...)` for the legacy store), but they never call `m.AssertExpectations(t)` (or otherwise wait for/verify the goroutine ran). Because the legacy call happens in a goroutine, the test can complete before that call occurs, so the new async legacy dual-write behavior is effectively untested. This is a concrete test coverage gap tied to the new async behavior, not a direct production defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Update no longer fetches old object and computes UpdatedObject/wraps in updateWrapper, passing raw objInfo to legacy Update, changing what legacy storage receives and validation semantics, without test coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the previous logic that fetched the old object (`d.Storage.Get`), computed `objInfo.UpdatedObject(...)`, and wrapped `objInfo` in an `updateWrapper` before calling `d.Legacy.Update` was removed. The new code calls `d.Storage.Update(...)` directly and then asynchronously calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` with the *raw* `objInfo` (no `updateWrapper`), which can change what legacy storage sees and how/when `UpdatedObject` is computed. The new `TestMode3_Update` uses mocks with `mock.Anything` for the `objInfo` argument and does not assert that legacy receives the wrapped/updated object, so it does not cover the semantic change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Delete no longer tolerates apierrors.IsNotFound from unified storage and returns immediately, breaking deletes when unified storage is missing an object that exists in legacy

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Delete previously treated a unified-store Delete error of apierrors.IsNotFound as non-fatal (it only returned early for non-NotFound), and still proceeded to delete from Legacy. The new implementation returns immediately on any error from d.Storage.Delete (no IsNotFound check), and only triggers legacy delete in the async goroutine on success. This will break deletion when the unified store is missing the object but legacy still has it, exactly as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Delete records storage duration with object name instead of options.Kind as the kind label, producing inconsistent metric labels
matched_golden_ids: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments describe the same inconsistency in metrics labeling: the code records metrics using the object name rather than options.Kind for the kind label, leading to inconsistent metric labels compared to other methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: No test coverage for legacy-write failure while storage succeeds or the 10s WithTimeoutCause timeout firing; timeout and metric-recording paths have zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new, nontrivial async legacy-write behavior in Mode3 (e.g., `Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection` now spawn a goroutine that uses `context.WithTimeoutCause(..., 10s, ...)` and calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)`). The new tests in `dualwriter_mode3_test.go` primarily exercise storage success/failure paths and do not verify legacy-write failure handling or the timeout/metrics paths (no assertions around legacy goroutine execution, no simulated long-running legacy call, and no expectations/assertions on `recordLegacyDuration`/timeout behavior). Thus the finding about zero coverage for these new paths is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: TestMode3_Create failure case is mislabeled — only setupLegacyFn is configured and the storage mock is unset, so the intended unified-store failure path is not genuinely exercised

adjudication.rationale: In `TestMode3_Create`, the failure case labeled "error when creating object in the unified store fails" only configures `setupLegacyFn` (`m.On("Create", ...).Return(nil, errors.New("error"))`) and does not configure `setupStorageFn`. But `DualWriterMode3.Create` calls `d.Storage.Create(...)` first and returns that error; legacy create happens only after storage succeeds (and asynchronously). So the test does not genuinely exercise the intended unified-store failure path and is misleading/misconfigured (and may even fail due to an unexpected mock call on `Storage.Create`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Async legacy writes in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection derive their 10s-timeout context from the request ctx, which is canceled when the HTTP response is written, so fire-and-forget legacy writes will frequently be canceled before completing, silently diverging legacy vs unified storage

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3 the legacy operations are now executed in goroutines and create their 10s timeout context from the incoming `ctx` (e.g. `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...) ... d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection(ctx, ...) }`). If the caller cancels `ctx` when the main request finishes (typical for request-scoped contexts), the derived context will be canceled immediately/early, causing these fire-and-forget legacy writes to abort and silently diverge from unified storage (errors are not surfaced to the caller). This behavior is introduced by the diff changing legacy writes from synchronous to async and still chaining to the original `ctx`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update no longer reconciles the legacy write with the stored object: raw objInfo is passed to d.Legacy.Update instead of the updateWrapper carrying the object persisted to unified storage, so defaults/mutations (RV bump, normalization) never reach legacy, causing persistent divergence

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, Update was changed from computing an updated object and then calling Legacy.Update with an updateWrapper carrying the object actually persisted to Storage (the `obj` returned by `d.Storage.Update`) to instead calling `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` in a goroutine after `d.Storage.Update(...)` (see new code). This means legacy now receives the original `objInfo` rather than a wrapper that replays the exact stored object, so any mutations/defaulting/resourceVersion changes applied by the unified store result can be missed by legacy, leading to divergence. The diff shows the previous reconciliation via updateWrapper was removed and not replaced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy write failures are silently dropped with no logging; errors are only fed into a metric, removing the previous log.Error trace and making divergence undiagnosable in production

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, legacy writes were changed to async goroutines with timeouts (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). In these goroutines, errors from d.Legacy.* are not logged anymore (e.g., Create now just does `_, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Create(...)` and records a metric; previous code logged `log.WithValues(...).Error(err, ...)`). As a result, legacy write failures can be effectively silent from logs and only reflected in metrics, matching the finding. This is an observability/diagnosability regression rather than a direct functional correctness bug (mode 3 appears designed to not fail the request on legacy errors).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update error path calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) (~line 145) instead of recordStorageDuration, polluting the legacy latency metric with unified-storage failures
matched_golden_ids: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that in DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection error path, d.recordLegacyDuration(...) is called instead of recordStorageDuration, corrupting legacy metrics with storage failures—this matches the golden issue exactly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DeleteCollection legacy goroutine calls d.recordStorageDuration(...) (~line 175) instead of recordLegacyDuration, so the legacy metric never gets delete-collection data and the storage metric is double-counted

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, DeleteCollection records storage metrics for the legacy async write: inside the goroutine it calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` even though `startLegacy` measures the legacy call (`d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)`). This will misattribute legacy latency/errors to the storage metric and omit legacy delete-collection metrics (and potentially double-count storage).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete passes name instead of options.Kind as the metric label (~line 108), mixing object names with kinds and breaking label consistency/cardinality for successful deletes

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go` within `Delete`, the success path calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`, passing the object `name` where other metric recordings in this file consistently pass `options.Kind` as the label value (and the error path in the same function does pass `options.Kind`). This mixes label semantics and can explode label cardinality for successful deletes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Goroutines capture options/deleteValidation/objInfo and re-run createValidation/deleteValidation asynchronously after the response; if validations depend on request-scoped state or have side effects, behavior differs from the synchronous path

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes were changed from synchronous to asynchronous goroutines (e.g., `Create` launches `go func(){ d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, createValidation, options) }()`, `Delete` launches `d.Legacy.Delete(ctx, name, deleteValidation, options)`, `Update` launches `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, createValidation, updateValidation, ...)`). This necessarily reuses/captures `options`, `objInfo`, and the validation funcs after the main call has returned, changing behavior vs the previous synchronous path and potentially being unsafe if those funcs/objects rely on request-scoped context/state or are not intended to be invoked asynchronously/after response. The diff shows this change clearly, but whether it manifests as a concrete defect depends on how those callbacks are implemented/used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Massive duplication of the timing/logging/async pattern across five methods, which already introduced copy-paste bugs (wrong recorder, wrong label); a writeToLegacyAsync helper would prevent these

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows repeated copy/paste timing/async patterns in DualWriterMode3 that already contain concrete mistakes: e.g., Create() records `recordLegacyDuration(...)` on a Storage.Create error using `startStorage` (should be storage recorder), Update() does the same on Storage.Update error, DeleteCollection()’s legacy goroutine calls `recordStorageDuration(...)` instead of legacy, and Delete() calls `recordStorageDuration(false, ..., name, ...)` using `name` where other paths use `options.Kind` (label mismatch). These are verifiable correctness/metrics bugs arising from duplicated code, so a helper would prevent them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests reuse a shared package-level p registry while TestMode3_Get creates a fresh local one; if the shared registry is a package global reused across test functions, metric registration may panic with duplicate metrics collector registration

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent Prometheus registry usage across tests: `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode1_test.go` removes `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` but still calls `NewDualWriter(..., p)`, implying `p` is now coming from a package-level/shared variable. In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, most tests also call `NewDualWriter(..., p)` without defining `p`, while `TestMode3_Get` explicitly creates a fresh `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()`. If `NewDualWriter` registers collectors into the provided registry, reusing a shared registry across multiple tests can cause duplicate registration panics; the diff doesn’t prove that panic occurs, but it does create/reflect a concrete cross-test coupling risk and inconsistency grounded in the changed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mode3Str const is declared after first use (~line 33) and the mode string is duplicated per mode file, adding per-method metric-label plumbing as more mode files are added

adjudication.rationale: In Go, package-scope identifiers (like `const mode3Str = "3"`) can be referenced before their textual declaration in the same file, so `newDualWriterMode3(...).WithValues("mode", mode3Str)` compiling/working is not a verifiable defect from this diff. The claim about the mode string being duplicated across mode files and increasing per-method metric-label plumbing is not shown in this diff (only Mode3 is visible), and is too speculative/vague to verify here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Async legacy write goroutines derive timeout context from the incoming request context, which is cancelled when the response returns, aborting legacy writes mid-flight and causing intermittent silent divergence between unified and legacy storage (pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go)

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes are executed in goroutines using `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` where `ctx` is the incoming request context (e.g., in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). Because the goroutine context is derived from the request context, any cancellation/deadline on the original ctx will immediately propagate and can abort the async legacy write. The goroutine also does not log the legacy error (it only records duration metrics), so aborted legacy writes can lead to silent divergence between Storage and Legacy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Delete runs legacy deleteValidation after the object is already gone from unified storage, so validation functions inspecting current state can fail or behave differently, silently skipping the legacy delete and causing permanent divergence

adjudication.rationale: In Mode3 Delete, unified storage is deleted first (`d.Storage.Delete(...)`), then legacy delete is executed asynchronously with the same `deleteValidation` (`go func() { ... d.Legacy.Delete(ctx, name, deleteValidation, options) ... }()`). Any error from the legacy delete (including validation failures) is neither returned nor logged, so the legacy delete can effectively be skipped silently, leaving legacy and unified storage diverged. The finding’s exact claim about validation depending on unified-store current state is speculative, but the diff does introduce silent legacy-delete failure after US delete, which can cause permanent divergence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Update passes the raw objInfo to Legacy.Update instead of wrapping it with the previously fetched old object and the updated result, breaking conflict detection/resourceVersion handling and optimistic-concurrency checks in legacy storage

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the old implementation explicitly fetched the current object from `Storage`, computed `updated := objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old)`, and then wrapped `objInfo` in an `updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: ...}` before calling both `Storage.Update` and `Legacy.Update`. The new code removes the pre-`Get`/precompute/wrapper entirely and calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` directly (in the async goroutine) after `d.Storage.Update(...)`. This is exactly what the finding describes: legacy no longer receives the wrapper carrying the already-updated object, so legacy may recompute updates against its own state rather than applying the same updated result, potentially affecting resourceVersion/conflict semantics that the wrapper previously enforced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Legacy write failures are fully silent — errors only feed a metric counter, never logged or surfaced, so requests report success while unified and legacy stores diverge

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes are moved to background goroutines for `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection` and their errors are not logged or returned. The goroutines only call `recordLegacyDuration(...)` (and in `DeleteCollection` even calls `recordStorageDuration(...)` inside the legacy goroutine) but do not `log.Error(...)` on failure. Previously (before this diff) legacy operation failures were logged (e.g., `log.WithValues(...).Error(err, ...)`), so this diff creates an observability regression where legacy failures can be effectively silent aside from metrics, while the request still returns success based on unified store results.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Update error branch calls recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration (pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go)

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go` within `(*DualWriterMode3).Update`, the error path after `d.Storage.Update(...)` fails calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. That duration corresponds to the unified store (storage) operation (`startStorage` taken before `d.Storage.Update`), so it should record a storage metric (i.e., `recordStorageDuration`), not a legacy metric. This makes the metrics incorrect and misattributes storage failures to legacy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration for the legacy delete instead of recordLegacyDuration

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection`, the async legacy write path incorrectly records the legacy duration via `d.recordStorageDuration(...)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)`: inside the `go func()` it does `_, err := d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)` followed by `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`. This is inconsistent with the other legacy goroutines in the same file (e.g., `Create/Delete/Update`) which call `recordLegacyDuration` for legacy operations, and would misattribute legacy timings to the storage metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Delete success path passes name to recordStorageDuration where other call sites pass options.Kind, corrupting the kind label cardinality/semantics

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Delete, the success path calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`, passing `name` where all other call sites consistently pass `options.Kind` as the third argument (e.g., Create/Get/List/Delete error path/DeleteCollection). This strongly indicates the third parameter is intended to be the resource kind label; using `name` would corrupt metrics semantics and likely explode label cardinality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Every write path spawns an unbounded detached goroutine with no semaphore, no panic recovery, and no mechanism to propagate legacy write failures; a panic inside Legacy.* or a validation fn crashes the process

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, the Mode3 write methods (`Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `DeleteCollection`) now launch a detached `go func(){... d.Legacy.* ...}()` for the legacy write with only a 10s timeout and no concurrency limit or panic recovery. A panic in `d.Legacy.*` (or code it calls, including validation funcs passed through) would panic the goroutine and crash the whole process (no `recover`). Legacy errors are also not propagated to the caller (they’re ignored aside from duration recording), so failures are silent from the API perspective. This behavior is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: New tests only assert unified-store results and never assert LegacyStorage.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection was invoked or legacy failure handling, so the suite passes while legacy writes are broken; async legacy writes are also unsynchronized, making spy assertions flaky

adjudication.rationale: In the new `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go` tests, assertions are only about the returned object/list from the unified `Storage` calls (e.g., `assert.Equal(t, obj, exampleObj)`), and there are no checks that `LegacyStorage.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection` were invoked or that legacy-error handling works. Although some tests set up legacy `m.On(...)` expectations, they never call `m.AssertExpectations(t)` (or otherwise verify call counts), so the suite can pass even if legacy writes never happen. The production code also performs legacy operations asynchronously via `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection ... }()`, so adding call assertions later would require synchronization to avoid flakiness, aligning with the finding's concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Tests use the shared package-level p Prometheus registry in most Mode3 tests (only TestMode3_Get creates its own registry), causing cross-test metric contamination and inconsistent hygiene

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go, most tests call `NewDualWriter(Mode3, ls, us, p)` without defining `p` locally (implying a shared package-level registry), while `TestMode3_Get` explicitly creates `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()`. This inconsistency is visible in the diff and is a concrete test-isolation/hygiene issue that can lead to cross-test metric state leakage or duplicate registration problems if `NewDualWriter` registers collectors into the provided registry.
